ga4_sample.label: GA4 sample: Google Merchandise Store
ga4_sample.description: Google's public GA4 sample export (bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce): real store traffic, obfuscated by Google. No user_id, so every person is one device; revenue and some values are obfuscated, so the numbers show the pipeline working, not how Google's store performed.

tagline_site.label: Tagline Supply: the site's own GA4 export
tagline_site.description: The tagged React storefront's own GA4 property, exported daily to BigQuery. Every visit, order and account in it is synthetic: seeded simulator shoppers driving the real site in Chrome on one machine. Campaign spend is synthetic too.

tagline_site.scope: all attributed orders (none has a complete 30-day lookback)

expectations.expectation: GA4 sample: the Google Merchandise Store, tagged by Google, not to the Tagline contract, and obfuscated: currency and value only from add_shipping_info on, no items on add_shipping_info / add_payment_info, often none on view_item, item brand / quantity / list index often (not set), 450 purchases with no transaction_id
GA4 sample: obfuscated sources (<Other>, (data deleted)), and sessions with no source collected at all
GA4 sample: 324 purchase events repeat an earlier one of the same order on the same device; fct_orders keeps the first
GA4 sample: 15 transaction ids were sent from two devices weeks apart; kept as separate orders

pipeline_runs.note: One Airflow run of the daily DAG (airflow dags test) each, measured by the stage that made it. List price before free tiers: BigQuery on demand $6.25 per TiB billed, Dataproc Serverless $0.06 per DCU-hour.

runs.label: Stage 4: daily incremental build + tuned batch
Stage 5: + monitoring marts, 11 checks, alert tasks

monthly.text: A daily run for a month at list price, before and after Stage 4. BigQuery stays inside its free monthly tier either way, so what the project pays is the Spark part.

source.label: STAGE4-RESULTS.md, What it costs a month

backtest.text: Every alert was checked against the marts and judged: 12 incidents (the same series or event on consecutive days), 11 of them six real problems in the sample's own data, 1 noise. Christmas stayed inside the band.

judged.label: Purchases sent twice per order from the same device
The category quirk at a new high on a quiet Sunday
One-day glitch: purchases without a transaction id
The purchase tag breaks: no transaction id, checkout-to-purchase falls to 0

tag_qa.text: Scripted journeys in Chrome, checked against the contract and the rules, golden dataLayer snapshots and a GA4 hit layer, on every push in CI. The breaks were made to the site's tag code one at a time.

alert_history.text: On the site today only contract_violation and no_data can fire: the floor needs a day of 100 sessions (the site's day had 48), vanished needs 3 days of history, and the band 14 judged days, a day being judged only when it has enough volume.

consent_denied_orders.text: A purchase sent with consent denied has no device or session id, so it is an order in no session: it counts in orders and revenue, but has no campaign and no journey to attribute.

source.label: README.md, Results on the site's export

synthetic.text: Campaign spend (campaign_costs) and product unit costs are seeded and flagged in their tables; every row of the site's export comes from the simulator.

self_referral.text: A self-referral: the store's own domain referring to itself. It is mostly the last step of a journey that started elsewhere, so every multi-touch model moves part of its credit back to where the buyer came from.
